predecessors.note: Infobox 'Preceded by: Yang Tong of Sui (Central Jiangsu)'. 'After Emperor Yang was killed in the spring of 618 at Jiangdu'; Chen Leng held Jiangdu until Li took it in fall 619.

land.text: Shen Faxing's former lands, 'roughly modern Zhejiang' (Li Zitong page), with Piling (Changzhou); Jiangdu (Yangzhou) no longer held after 620; capital Yuhang (Hangzhou)

successors.note: Infobox 'Succeeded by: Emperor Gaozu of Tang'. 'In winter 621, Li Fuwei sent Wang Xiongdan against Li Zitong', defeating him at Hangzhou; Li surrendered and was sent to Chang'an. Li Fuwei is Du Fuwei, the Tang's Prince of Wu. Jiangdu is not in this land: Li Zitong abandoned it in 620 and 'modern central and southern Jiangsu came under Li Fuwei's control' (Du Fuwei page).

rulers.note: Surrendered winter 621, executed 622 after fleeing from Chang'an and being arrested at Lantian Pass.

correction.text: Shen Faxing's former lands, 'roughly modern Zhejiang' (Li Zitong page), with Piling (Changzhou); Jiangdu (Yangzhou) no longer held after 620; capital Yuhang (Hangzhou)

keyframe_review.note: Redrawn after review: 'Shen Faxing's former lands (roughly modern Zhejiang)' with Piling (Changzhou), capital Yuhang (Hangzhou), and no Jiangdu. The Li Zitong page dates the whole sequence to 620 (it begins 'In 620, Li crossed the Yangtze to attack Shen'; he 'abandoned Jiangdu, heading first to Jingkou') and its infobox gives Emperor of China (Central Jiangsu) 619-620, (Southern Jiangsu) 620, (Zhejiang) 620-621; the Du Fuwei page agrees ('Li Zitong abandoned Jiangdu and fled to Jingkou', after Du's summer 620 title change). Neither page gives a month, so the Jiangdu disc is dropped for the whole of 620. No area on the page.

ledger.note: Fall 619: Li Zitong takes Jiangdu and claims Wu. 'In the fall of 619, Li put Jiangdu, then controlled by Chen, under siege. Li captured the city, and he then claimed the title of Emperor of Wu.'

region.text: 'Zhejiang and southern Jiangsu, including Jiangnan' (Shen Faxing page infobox), capital Piling (modern Changzhou)

ledger.note: 620: Li Zitong takes Shen Faxing's lands. 'In 620, Li crossed the Yangtze to attack Shen, who had his capital at Piling. Shen later committed suicide, and Li took over Shen's territory, roughly modern Zhejiang.'

620: Li Zitong abandons Jiangdu. 'after he ran out of food supplies, he abandoned Jiangdu, heading first to Jingkou' while Li Fuwei's (Du Fuwei's) generals Fu Gongshi, Kan Leng and Wang Xiongdan attacked him; the Li Zitong page infobox ends 'Central Jiangsu' at 620 and dates the whole sequence to 620. Second page (Du Fuwei): 'Li Zitong abandoned Jiangdu and fled to Jingkou', after Du became the Tang's Prince of Wu in summer 620, and 'modern central and southern Jiangsu came under Li Fuwei's control'. Counterpart is tang-dynasty because the attacker was by then the Tang's Prince of Wu; the du-fuwei-s-regime dossier ends at that title change. No month on either page.

region.text: Shen Faxing's former lands, 'roughly modern Zhejiang' (Li Zitong page), with Piling (Changzhou); Jiangdu (Yangzhou) no longer held after 620; capital Yuhang (Hangzhou)

ledger.note: Winter 621: Li Zitong is defeated at Hangzhou. 'In winter 621, Li Fuwei sent Wang Xiongdan against Li Zitong. Wang's feigned larger army caused Li to panic, and Wang defeated him at Hangzhou.' Li surrendered and was sent to Chang'an; fleeing in 622 he was arrested at Lantian Pass and executed. The land passes to the Tang through Li Fuwei (Du Fuwei). The land passed is the 620-621 shape (Zhejiang and Piling); Jiangdu had been lost in 620.

wars.note: The Li Zitong page has Li Fuwei (Du Fuwei, by then a Tang prince) send the generals in 620 and Wang Xiongdan again in winter 621; the Tang itself is not shown fighting. Extended from 621 to 620 after review, because the 620 loss of Jiangdu came out of this campaign.

notes: Rebel state Cliopatria lacks; slug li-zitong-s-wu as ea-03-f suggested. The page gives no month; the Tang is not shown fighting: Li Fuwei (Du Fuwei) is the Tang's Prince of Wu, so counterpart tang-dynasty is the researcher's reading. The Li Zitong page gives 619 for Jiangdu while the infobox says the territory reaches Zhejiang only after 620. Overlaps with du-fuwei-s-regime (616-620) in the lower Yangtze; the compiler must settle the order. Sub-year-limit state; written because ea-03-f asked. Review fix (ea-03-x): Jiangdu is lost in 620 (Li Zitong and Du Fuwei pages), so the 620-621 keyframe, the successor land and the 621 dissolve region are Zhejiang plus the Piling (Changzhou) disc, and a 620 loss of Yangzhou (70 km) to tang-dynasty is in the ledger. The pages give no month. The loss names tang-dynasty, not du-fuwei-s-regime, because the Du Fuwei page puts the attack after his summer 620 title change (Prince of Wu), where the du-fuwei-s-regime dossier already dissolves into the Tang; tang-dynasty (ea-04) should carry the matching gain and the vassal tint for Li Fuwei.
